outputs.L1: Method for visualizing a tooth situation. The invention relates to a method for visualizing a tooth situation, wherein an image of a patient’s face is recorded and stored as a facial data record (1). Feature points (3) within the facial data record (1) are automatically recognized by means of a facial recognition method. A mouth area (4) located between the lips is automatically recognized on the basis of the feature points (3). A position of the face in the facial data record (1) and a three-dimensional direction (5) of an orientation of the face in the facial data record (1) are automatically recognized on the basis of the feature points (3). A virtual tooth data record (2) of the tooth situation is oriented according to the three-dimensional direction (5) of the orientation of the face and positioned according to the position of the face with respect to the facial data record (1). The mouth area within the facial data record (1) is partially overlaid and/or overlaid and/or replaced by the tooth data record (2), and the result is displayed as a visualization data record.
outputs.L2: A technique for depicting a dental condition is described. In this method, an image of a patient’s face is captured and saved as a face dataset (1). Using facial-recognition processing, feature points (3) in the face dataset (1) are identified automatically. Based on these feature points (3), the system automatically detects the mouth region (4) between the lips. The same feature points (3) are also used to automatically determine both the position of the face in the face dataset (1) and the three-dimensional orientation direction (5) of the face. A virtual dental dataset (2) representing the dental condition is then aligned with the three-dimensional facial orientation direction (5) and placed relative to the face position within the face dataset (1). The mouth region in the face dataset (1) is then partly covered, covered, and/or substituted with the dental dataset (2), and the resulting image is shown as a visualization dataset.
outputs.L3:
The method provides a visualization of a patient’s tooth situation by first recording and storing an image of the patient’s face. This recorded image is stored as a facial data record and serves as the basis for the subsequent visualization process.

Using a facial recognition method, facial feature points are automatically identified within the facial data record. These feature points may include characteristic points of the face, such as points around the eyes, nose, lips, jawline, or other recognizable facial structures.

Based on the recognized facial feature points, the system automatically determines the mouth area located between the lips. In addition, the position of the face within the facial data record and the three-dimensional orientation of the face are determined. This makes it possible to identify not only where the face is located in the image, but also how the face is spatially oriented, for example whether it is turned, tilted, or inclined.

A virtual tooth data record is then aligned with the determined three-dimensional orientation of the face. The tooth data record is also positioned in accordance with the detected face position in the facial data record. As a result, the virtual tooth data can be placed in a spatially correct relationship to the patient’s face.

The mouth area in the facial image is then partially overlaid, fully overlaid, or replaced by the tooth data record. This produces a visualization data record in which the virtual tooth situation is shown in relation to the patient’s face. The resulting visualization data record is displayed, allowing the tooth situation to be viewed realistically in the context of the patient’s facial appearance.
outputs.L4:
The method provides a way to visualize a patient’s dental situation in direct relation to the patient’s face. For this purpose, an image of the patient’s face is first recorded, for example by means of a camera or another suitable imaging device. The facial image is then analyzed automatically in order to identify characteristic facial feature points. These feature points may include, for example, the corners of the eyes, the nose, the chin, the lips, the corners of the mouth, and other landmarks that make it possible to determine the position, orientation, and proportions of the face.

Using the detected facial feature points, the system determines the location of the mouth area within the facial image. The mouth area may be defined as the region containing the lips, teeth, and surrounding soft tissue. In addition, the system determines the spatial orientation of the face, including its three-dimensional pose, such as rotation, inclination, and viewing angle relative to the camera. This makes it possible to establish how the patient’s head is positioned at the time the image is captured.

A virtual tooth data record is then provided. This tooth data record may represent the patient’s actual dental situation, for example based on an intraoral scan, a dental model, a three-dimensional tooth model, a planned restoration, an orthodontic treatment result, or another digital representation of the teeth. The tooth data record is aligned with the detected position of the mouth and with the determined three-dimensional orientation of the patient’s face. In this way, the virtual teeth are transformed, scaled, rotated, and positioned so that they correspond to the patient’s facial image as accurately as possible.

After alignment, the tooth data record is displayed together with the facial image. Depending on the intended application, the virtual tooth data may be overlaid onto the existing mouth area or may replace part or all of the mouth area in the recorded image. For example, the original teeth shown in the photograph may be covered by the virtual tooth representation, while the surrounding facial features remain visible. This produces a realistic visualization of how the patient’s teeth appear, or would appear, within the context of the patient’s own face.

The resulting image therefore combines the facial photograph with accurately oriented dental data. Because the tooth data is matched not only to the two-dimensional position of the mouth but also to the three-dimensional orientation of the face, the visualization can provide a more natural and precise representation than a simple image overlay. The method can be used to document an existing dental condition, to preview a proposed dental restoration, to simulate orthodontic or cosmetic treatment, or to support communication between a dentist, dental technician, and patient.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention about visualizing a patient’s tooth situation by overlaying virtual tooth data onto a facial image using facial recognition feature points.
counterfactuals.output: A method and system for visualizing a patient-specific dental condition are disclosed. A facial image of a patient is acquired and analyzed to identify facial recognition feature points, including points associated with the mouth, lips, and other facial landmarks. Virtual tooth data representing one or more teeth, a dental arch, a proposed restoration, an orthodontic arrangement, or a treatment outcome is obtained and spatially aligned with the facial image based at least in part on the identified feature points. The aligned virtual tooth data is overlaid onto the facial image to generate a composite visualization showing the patient’s tooth situation in relation to the patient’s face. The system may adjust scale, position, orientation, and perspective of the virtual tooth data according to the facial feature points and may display the composite visualization for diagnosis, treatment planning, patient communication, or simulation of dental outcomes.

counterfactuals.output: A dental augmented-reality system and method are provided for generating a real-time visualization of a dental restoration or cosmetic dental treatment. counterfactuals.output:
**Method for visualizing a tooth situation**

A method for visualizing a tooth situation comprises acquiring at least one image or video stream of a patient’s face, automatically recognizing facial features therein, and detecting the lip and/or mouth region to determine a visible oral opening. Based on the recognized facial landmarks, a three-dimensional orientation and pose of the face is determined relative to an imaging device, and a virtual tooth dataset, such as a digital dental model, planned restoration, orthodontic setup, or simulated tooth arrangement, is spatially aligned with the detected mouth region. The method further includes overlaying the virtual tooth dataset onto the facial image in accordance with the determined 3D face orientation so that the virtual teeth are displayed in a realistic position behind or within the lips, thereby enabling visualization of a current, planned, or alternative tooth situation in a patient-specific facial context.
